content: I'll read the test image first, then the part index, then view reference images for my top candidates.

The image shows whole plant + stem involvement. Top candidates based on pale bleached stems, wilting, and root exposure: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt. Viewing one reference per candidate.
Sclerotinia shows pale bleached stems with sclerotia and white mycelium - very similar to the test image. Now checking Southern_Blight.

Bacterial Wilt shows bacterial streaming and field wilting but stems don't match the pale bleached appearance. Now checking Verticillium_Wilt for my 4th reference.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Whole tomato plant pulled from soil, showing extensively pale/bleached white-tan stems throughout their length, wilting/browned leaves, brownish-reddish roots, and overall plant collapse.

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: Reference image 5530074 showed pale bleached stem tissue very similar to the test image - extensive whitish bleaching along stems, with embedded dark structures. This is the best match.

- **Southern_Blight**: Shows white mycelium concentrated at the soil line/crown. Somewhat similar presentation (pulled plant) but bleaching less extensive up the stem.

- **Bacterial_Wilt**: Shows bacterial streaming in water and field wilting, but stems don't show the pale bleaching pattern.

- **Verticillium_Wilt**: Shows V-shaped leaf lesions and vascular streaking in stem cross-section — doesn't match the extensive external stem bleaching.

The pale/bleached straw-colored stems extending up the plant length most closely match Sclerotinia Timber Rot, which is known for causing extensive stem bleaching with internal hollow/white mycelium and black sclerotia.
